dedupe_keys.name: dar es salaam ai mapping of solid waste in waterways and flood risk

description: This case study maps municipal solid waste across Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, with an artificial intelligence workflow, because waste that blocks drains and waterways amplifies urban flooding in fast-growing African cities. The authors, from Heidelberg University's GIScience group with local partners, published it as a preprint. The workflow detects waste at high resolution in openly available aerial and street-view imagery, with labels produced together with local partners to reflect real reuse practices, and relates waste patterns to informal settlements and socio-economic factors. Coverage is the city of Dar es Salaam. The preprint is free to read and download on arXiv. Caveats: detection accuracy depends on image dates and coverage, the labelled data and model availability are not stated in the abstract, and flood effects are inferred from waste locations, not modelled hydraulically. The study found waste accumulation in waterways up to three times higher than in adjacent urban areas, identifying hotspots where climate-exacerbated flooding is most likely, and argues the approach allows city-wide monitoring and prioritised interventions. Simulation uses: adding drainage blockage from waste to urban flood hazard exposure models, and targeting waste collection for climate adaptation. Related records: the UN-Habitat Waste Wise Cities Tool (platform-un-habitat-waste-wise-cities-tool) supports city waste assessments and What a Waste (data-what-a-waste-global-database) gives national waste statistics.
